---
title: "Native data structures and cellular geometry"
---

Cellerator separates reusable dependency knowledge, concrete numerical data
representations and their execution bindings. These building blocks work
without a `Cell`, model superclass, Python runtime or universal tensor facade.
The [cellular geometry definition](cellular_geometry.qmd) supplies the design
authority; physical packing does not establish a biological restriction.

## Native boundaries

| Namespace | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `structure` | Persistent domain/order/entity/occurrence identities and logical axes; runtime registry handles remain in execution. |
| `geometry::dependency` | Applicability, possible explicit/implicit participant patterns, declared condition inputs and the scope of dependency knowledge. |
| `containers` | Reusable storage/count/shape primitives without biological or scheduling meaning. |
| `tensor` | Concrete specialist encodings with typed views and separate owners. Ordinary dense/CSR/COO use established libraries or caller storage. |
| `layout` | Physical permutations, local coordinate maps, immutable projections and canonical/gradient recovery. |
| `memory::cuda` | Explicit-device resources, borrowing and allocation lifetime. |
| `ops` | Numerical computation, access/effects, derivative requests and operation-specific omission contracts. |
| `execution` | Prepared source association, current work, generations, retained contents, readiness and device realization. |

Canonical semantic identity is defined in
`<Cellerator/structure/identity.hh>`. An entity ID, occurrence ID, logical
coordinate and physical slot are different concepts. Domain-local zero is a
valid entity/occurrence ID; an all-zero persistent domain identity is invalid.
Matching counts or pointers do not establish matching logical order.

## Patterns, conditions and actual operations

`geometry::dependency::ExplicitPattern` owns ordered/repeated participant
incidence and its prepared postings. `PatternOwner` publishes structural
snapshots. `JointGroups`, `CartesianPattern` and `UnionPattern` can describe
possible interactions without first enumerating every pair. A `FoundationView`
also declares applicability, coverage and whether its knowledge is a model
restriction, established restriction, prior or hint. Partial knowledge cannot
justify deleting otherwise admitted computation.

The model defines and evaluates its conditions. `ConditionReads` identifies
their required sources. An `ops::mechanism::AccessContract` states actual reads,
writes, output effects and phase-specific needs. An omission rule is tied to
that operation, revision, selected membership, outcome, numerical semantics and
supported derivative order. Reusing a selection ID with different membership
does not broaden a certificate.

The concrete `PreparedGatedProductBinding` binds one joint-operation family to
source domains/orders, condition/participant selections and scoped omission
rules. Its coordinate domain is explicitly associated with source axes;
preparation does not invent biological entity identities from array positions.

`execution::PreparedConditionIndex` indexes the selections read by conditions.
`ConditionState` tracks source and time revisions, invalidates affected cached
outcomes and rejects stale or reused evaluation tickets. Unaffected outcomes
can remain cached. These stamps do not pin numerical contents or establish
device readiness; the source owner still supplies those guarantees.

The example operation is a baseline plus conditionally gated, ordered products
with overlapping output contributions. Its squared-positive-part gate has an
explicit inactive branch and first-order derivative contract. That permits
specific participant work to be skipped; a generic learned numerical zero
does not imply the same derivative omission. The host forward returns an
owning one-shot tape. The [native C++ model interface](native_nn.qmd) remains
ordinary structs/callables and can consume these facilities directly.

For example, a host model can share prepared geometry and keep ordinary typed
parameter storage. Its instance supplies values and their logical association:

```cpp
namespace mech = cellerator::ops::mechanism;
namespace dep = cellerator::geometry::dependency;

struct Samples {
    std::size_t batch;
    std::span<const float> expression, regulators;
    std::span<const dep::SourceDescriptor> sources;
};

struct GeometryModel {
    std::shared_ptr<const mech::PreparedGatedProductBinding> geometry;
    std::vector<float> theta, phi, tau;

    auto operator()(const Samples& samples) const {
        if (!geometry->validate_sources(samples.sources))
            throw std::invalid_argument("incompatible logical sources");
        return mech::gated_product_forward(
            geometry->topology(), samples.batch,
            samples.expression, samples.regulators, theta, phi, tau, 0.25f);
    }
};
```

The result contains values and an owning tape for
`mech::gated_product_backward`. A `Cell` may bind this callable to an instance;
direct and batched callers use the same types. The host reference snapshots
needed inputs. Device execution uses retained reads and completion events
instead. The checked [host example](../tests/native_data/reference/native_data_reference_test.cc)
and [two-device example](../tests/execution_dependency/distributed_cuda_test.cu)
exercise the complete preparation and gradient paths.

## Concrete storage and physical realization

`tensor::block_masked::Structure` owns immutable host row/feature maps,
tile/block offsets and masks. A `LayoutView` borrows format metadata; a typed
`View<T>` adds numerical storage. Allocated masks describe valid stored slots,
including numerical zeros. A missing required coordinate is an error, not a
value inferred to be zero.

`DeviceStructure` owns a device-local immutable metadata replica.
`NativeTensor<T>` owns a bulk value allocation and exposes explicit reads and
edits. A retained read pins actual published contents through its consumers;
an unresolved read prevents in-place edits. Allocation retention or a
generation counter alone cannot preserve values overwritten before backward.
The execution owner retains reads through actual CUDA completion.

Codebook values live in `tensor::state_codes`; affine low-bit sparse views live
in `tensor::quantized`. They have different encodings. Useful persisted legacy
payloads have explicit format codecs; native namespace moves do not silently
reinterpret serialized bytes. A logical group need not have an allocation of
its own, and overlapping groups need not duplicate canonical values.

Logical occurrence coordinates and their order token live in `structure`.
`layout::OccurrenceMap` supplies a separate physical association, and
`layout::AxisBinding` associates a logical axis with its realization.
`execution::FeatureSourceBinding` owns the prepared source-to-model mapping;
biological labels and annotations remain in `biology`.

`layout::EntityLayout` and projection maps retain physical addressing/recovery.
`execution::PreparedIncidence` holds prepared addressing; numerical
gather/reduce/scatter live in `ops::incidence`. A prepared read index can reuse
one semantic posting owner while producing an explicit compact device ordinal
projection. That projection has preparation and memory cost of its own.
The [CellPack bridge](development/cellpack_interop.md) retains existing payload
encodings while separating physical summaries from live execution bindings.

## Connected execution

The existing execution machinery supplies atom requirements, logical coverage,
multi-extent ports, structural/value planes, output effects and prepared
programs. Dependency bindings associate semantic sources with these contracts.
Streams, current values, workspace and readiness remain invocation state.

`execution::dependency::DeviceExtentBinding` checks identity/order, structure,
device/placement, value generation, readiness association and capacity.
The concrete `PreparedDistributedGatedProduct` demonstrates a connected
two-device realization. The caller chooses two device ordinals and group
ownership. This bounded operation fixes expression/output/parameter homes at
device slot 0 and regulator home at slot 1; it is not a general placement or
population scheduler.

Preparation requires explicit physical-order identities independently of
logical order. Canonical row IDs map to batch ordinals; they are never used
directly as regulator-array offsets. The caller's device ordinals may differ
from physical inventory indices or logical owner slots.

Both devices consume native packed views. The bound flat-gate rule permits
condition-first participant projection. Inactive entries are not read; when
all remote participant work is inactive, its transfer is skipped. Mixed work
currently transfers the full prepared projection, including zero placeholders
for inactive entries. The tape retains forward contents, returns/reduces gradients to
their owners, and supports a canonical update with explicit replica refresh.
The scalar update changes theta only; explicit per-group learning rates can
also change gate parameters. Gate revisions are separate from theta revisions
so an unrelated parameter update does not invalidate participant projections.

This distributed realization requires output-producing groups and nonempty
participant coverage on each device. Unsupported topologies fail at
preparation; the more general host reference remains available for empty or
outputless compositions.

The first CUDA operation stores expression values in FP16, regulators and
parameters in FP32, and multiplies/accumulates/returns outputs and VJPs in
FP32. An explicit FP32 expression alternative remains available for local
operations. Declared precision and first-order scope bound these APIs; they
do not establish arbitrary higher-order or distributed autograd.

## Build and use

Host consumers use C++20 and an installed component:

```cmake
find_package(Cellerator REQUIRED COMPONENTS native_data)
target_link_libraries(my_model PRIVATE Cellerator::native_data)
```

`Cellerator::tensor` is the smaller host format surface. Optional
`Cellerator::native_data_cuda` composes CUDA owners and execution; these
dependencies are not required by host semantic headers. All package targets
require at least C++20, including CUDA translation units. Kernel-facing format
views remain ordinary header interfaces, but they do not define a separately
supported C++17 build lane. The package's C++20 `Cellerator::core_module`
target is built and exported normally; CUDA translation units continue to use
public headers rather than importing named modules.

Build the focused host checks without the unrelated compiler test suite:

```sh
cmake -S . -B /tmp/cellerator-native-data-host -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG_SCAN_DEPS=clang-scan-deps-18 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/anndatapp-install \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCELLERATOR_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
  -DCELLERATOR_BUILD_NATIVE_DATA_TESTS=ON
cmake --build /tmp/cellerator-native-data-host --target cellerator_native_data
ctest --test-dir /tmp/cellerator-native-data-host -R '^native_data_' --output-on-failure
```

GPU executables are buildable without being automatically launched by CTest.
Actual correctness, sanitizers and benchmarks require Scheduler admission.
Complete-cost comparisons include preparation, retained memory, projection
maintenance, movement, readiness, forward/backward and observable conversion.
The [implementation record](current_implementation.qmd) states demonstrated
coverage; API/source presence alone does not qualify a distributed capability
or performance claim.
